wageData.title: $15 an Hour is How Much a Year? ($31,200 Salary in 2026)
wageData.metaDescription: $15 an hour is $31,200 per year before taxes, or $2,600/mo and $1,200 biweekly for a 40-hour work week. See exact take-home pay after 2026 taxes.
wageData.h1: $15 an Hour is How Much a Year?
wageData.aeoDirectAnswer: Working 40 hours per week at **$15 an hour** equals an annual gross salary of **$31,200 per year** ($2,600 per month, $1,200 biweekly, or $600 per week). After standard 2026 Federal Income Tax ($1,754) and FICA ($2,386), your estimated net take-home pay is approximately **$27,060 per year** ($2,255/month) in zero-income-tax states like Texas or Florida.

faqs.q: $15 an hour is how much a year?
faqs.a: $15 an hour is $31,200 per year for a full-time employee working 40 hours per week (2,080 working hours in 52 weeks). If you take 2 weeks of unpaid vacation (2,000 hours), your annual gross earnings are $30,000.

faqs.q: How much is $15 an hour monthly?
faqs.a: At $15 per hour, your gross monthly pay is approximately $2,600 per month before taxes and deductions.
For employees paid every two weeks (26 paychecks per year), $15 an hour results in a gross biweekly paycheck of $1,200 (80 regular hours).

faqs.q: How much is $15 an hour after taxes?
faqs.a: After subtracting 2026 Federal Income Tax ($1,754) and FICA taxes ($2,386), a single filer takes home approximately $27,060 annually ($2,255/month or $1,041 biweekly) in states with no state income tax. In states like California or New York, state income tax will reduce net pay by an additional $780 to $936 per year.
